subject.name: Fjord Ledger
subject.audience: Bookkeepers at small Nordic shipping firms, working early mornings and late evenings in harbor offices
subject.primaryJob: Reconcile a month of entries at a time without ever doubting a number
sources: Tide tables: dense columns of times and heights, read at a glance
Ledger ruling: fine horizontal rules and column lines that keep figures aligned
Harbor office light: cold daylight off water at dawn, lamp light at dusk

principles: Sans-serif type, flush left, ragged right
Departs from generous white space: the ledger must show as much as possible without scrolling

territories.name: Harbor office
territories.description: The working office on a Nordic quay: tide tables pinned to the wall, ruled ledgers, cold water light through the window. Not the boats themselves.
territories.light: flat, cold daylight off water in the morning; low lamp light in the evening
territories.textures: none: flat surfaces and fine rules only
territories.composition: columns and rows on a strict grid, figures right-aligned
territories.motion: almost none: values change in place
territories.imagery: no imagery; data is the image

muse.name: Norwegian tide tables (Tidevannstabeller)
muse.take: the calm authority of a dense, ruled column of figures that you trust at a glance
muse.leave: the printed almanac look, nautical ornament and anchors

signature.concept: A full month on one screen
signature.reason: Tide tables and ledgers earn trust by showing every row at once; the brief asks for as much as possible without scrolling.

rationale.grounding.primary: Swiss International gives the grid and objective clarity of tide tables; reinterpreted because its airy space fights the no-scrolling brief.
rationale.territories.0: Harbor office, not harbor decoration: the brief says tide tables and ledger ruling, not maritime motifs.
rationale.color.anchors: Fjord blue from cold water light as primary; harbor grey for neutrals; ledger red for critical, the red ink of a ledger correction.
rationale.color.feedback: Independent: warnings and errors must read as feedback, never as the brand blue.
rationale.color.character.vibrancy: Muted: calm for long reconciliation sessions at dawn and dusk.
rationale.color.character.harmony: Unique: one accent, so nothing competes with the numbers.
rationale.color.character.neutral: Subtle: a trace of the cold water hue in the greys, less than the harbor canon's tint.
rationale.type.faces.display: Inter Tight: a neo-grotesque per the Swiss canon, tight enough for dense headers.
rationale.type.faces.body: Inter: neo-grotesque with tabular figures so columns of amounts align.
rationale.type.faces.utility: IBM Plex Mono for account codes and amounts, like the fixed columns of a tide table.
rationale.type.character.type-scale: Gentle: headings stay close to body so more rows fit; Swiss dramatic scale costs space.
rationale.form.scale: Small: more rows on one screen, from the no-scrolling brief.
rationale.form.density: Compact: the signature, from the tide table's dense columns.
rationale.form.space: Tight: gutters give way to rows; reinterprets Swiss airy space.
rationale.form.curvature: Crisp: precise edges, from the harbor canon and ledger ruling.
rationale.form.line: Hairline: ledger ruling separates rows and columns.
rationale.form.elevation: Flat: a ledger is one sheet, from the Swiss canon.
rationale.movement: Still: a number must never seem to move; from the Swiss canon and the precise, calm brief.
rationale.adaptivity: Both: bookkeepers work in morning daylight and late evening, so light and dark carry equal weight.
rationale.iconography: Lucide light: thin strokes that sit with hairline rules.

samples.error: Entry 214 is off by 120.00 NOK. Check the amount against the bank line.
